source_binding: Every command retains its exact source hashes, snapshots, patch, output, and exit code. The five named final checks match every committed Go file. The corrected prose check also matches the committed document. Earlier Go checks precede a paragraph-only formatting fix in that document. The original failed checks retain their original sources. Deleted source remains in the committed patch.
qualification: Local legacy migration rollback ownership, assembly identity binding, and CLI command compatibility. All twelve mapped CSP5 subcases remain unverified. No PR or merge credit.
limits: The previous goal turn made implementation progress at a05ca541 and recorded it in canonical commit 61d2d6f6. This turn continues CSP5 without reopening CSP4.

Seven original rollback scenarios fail with nine test failure events including parents. They cover unknown projected files, changed bytes with identical catalog semantics, replacement files, replacement roots, operator sidecars, and a replaced relocated store.

Rollback now uses the candidate inventory captured before publication. It verifies native file identities, content, and access before removing owned projected entries. Unknown or changed entries remain preserved.

The original store has a native directory identity captured before relocation. Both relocation and restoration use open parent directories and refuse every existing destination, including an empty directory.

Rollback retains projection-marker paths and the stable writer-lock file. Two existing tests now assert this preservation instead of expecting deletion of unowned entries. Tests still prove exact store restoration.
Cancellation uses a separate 30-second rollback context. The retained lock preserves its identity and excludes a concurrent writer after reuse.

Assembly initially accepted a replacement file containing identical bytes. Its separate failure test now passes after assembly compares the finished tree with the identities and bytes recorded during creation.

The first final prose check reports one eight-sentence paragraph. The corrected document splits that paragraph without changing its content or the writing policy. All 175 workspace and two CLI command test events pass with race instrumentation. Final ago, prose, Linux compilation, and Windows compilation pass. The CLI cases use their existing adapter fixture; workspace tests exercise real filesystem stores.
The native identity and candidate inventory remain in memory. They do not provide legacy relocation or workspace recovery after process exit.
Linux and Windows checks compile the workspace test binary. Native execution and physical power-loss behavior remain unqualified.

Legacy preflight still uses unbounded directory and manifest reads. Projection-marker temporary cleanup still uses an unchecked removal. These existing paths require bounded reads and ownership checks under CSP5.

Persistent workspace preparation and replacement recovery, active-writer exclusion, retained-evidence and discovery staging, generation retention, history compaction, the twelve mapped subcases, full verification, review, native CI, and merge remain open.

The first canonical prose check reports one long sentence and one nominalization. The corrected text preserves the same contract without policy changes. Both checks retain their original source and output. Plan maintenance preserves task criteria, invariants, scope, and the goal block.
